plan.title: Gender Equity in Physical Progress
plan.subtitle: Comparing baseline to endline performance improvements between boys and girls

panels.title: Total Girls Tracked
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT "Child ID" FROM "baseline" WHERE "Gender" = 'Female' UNION SELECT "Child ID" FROM "endline" WHERE "Gender" = 'Female') AS unique_girls

panels.title: Total Boys Tracked
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT "Child ID" FROM "baseline" WHERE "Gender" = 'Male' UNION SELECT "Child ID" FROM "endline" WHERE "Gender" = 'Male') AS unique_boys

panels.title: Avg Shuttle Run Improvement (Seconds)
panels.sql:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", "Shuttle run sec" AS baseline_val, NULL AS endline_val FROM "baseline"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", NULL AS baseline_val, "Shuttle run sec" AS endline_val FROM "endline"
),
matched AS (
  SELECT 
    c1."Gender",
    c1.baseline_val,
    c2.endline_val,
    (c1.baseline_val - c2.endline_val) AS improvement_sec
  FROM combined c1
  JOIN combined c2 ON c1."Child ID" = c2."Child ID" AND c1."Gender" = c2."Gender"
  WHERE c1.baseline_val IS NOT NULL AND c2.endline_val IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT "Gender", AVG(improvement_sec) AS avg_improvement FROM matched GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Avg Sit Ups Improvement (Count)
panels.sql:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", "Sit ups" AS baseline_val, NULL AS endline_val FROM "baseline"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", NULL AS baseline_val, "Sit ups" AS endline_val FROM "endline"
),
matched AS (
  SELECT 
    c1."Gender",
    c1.baseline_val,
    c2.endline_val,
    (c2.endline_val - c1.baseline_val) AS improvement_count
  FROM combined c1
  JOIN combined c2 ON c1."Child ID" = c2."Child ID" AND c1."Gender" = c2."Gender"
  WHERE c1.baseline_val IS NOT NULL AND c2.endline_val IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT "Gender", AVG(improvement_count) AS avg_improvement FROM matched GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Top 10 Improvers by Gender
panels.sql:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", "Shuttle run sec" AS baseline_val, NULL AS endline_val FROM "baseline"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", NULL AS baseline_val, "Shuttle run sec" AS endline_val FROM "endline"
),
matched AS (
  SELECT 
    c1."Child ID",
    c1."Gender",
    c1.baseline_val,
    c2.endline_val,
    (c1.baseline_val - c2.endline_val) AS shuttle_improvement
  FROM combined c1
  JOIN combined c2 ON c1."Child ID" = c2."Child ID" AND c1."Gender" = c2."Gender"
  WHERE c1.baseline_val IS NOT NULL AND c2.endline_val IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT "Child ID", "Gender", ROUND(shuttle_improvement, 2) AS shuttle_gain FROM matched ORDER BY shuttle_improvement DESC LIMIT 10

plan.narrative:
This dashboard compares the physical development of boys and girls from baseline to endline measurements. We track {{p1}} girls and {{p2}} boys who have complete records for both time periods.

In terms of speed and agility, measured by the shuttle run test, one gender shows an average improvement of {{p3.avg_improvement}} seconds, while the other improved by {{p3.avg_improvement}} seconds (note: lower time is better). This indicates whether the training program benefits one group more than the other in cardiovascular endurance.

For core strength, measured by sit-ups, the data reveals that one gender increased their average count by {{p4.avg_improvement}} repetitions compared to the other. A positive number here signifies a gain in muscle endurance over the program duration.

The table below highlights the top 10 individual performers across both genders based on shuttle run gains, allowing us to see if specific outliers are driving the averages or if the trend is consistent across the population.
